card: Immediately disconnects sockets in both the P2P networking loop and HTTP server when poll reports error or hangup events on connections where reads were paused. Previously, the node attempted a doomed send or read before disconnecting, causing redundant failed I/O calls and inaccurate debug logging. It also introduces dedicated functional tests covering TCP urgent data handling and peer resets during send stalls.
evidence: Commit ffeab17bae: 'On Linux a socket error or hangup is reported whichever events were requested. Disconnect directly when no read was requested, skipping the send attempt that would otherwise fail and disconnect the peer. This also changes the debug log message.'
Description: 'This just adds clarity: previously we would attempt a send that would then fail. The only side-effect is a changed log message.'
problem: On Linux, poll() reports POLLERR and POLLHUP events whether requested or not. When a peer or HTTP client connection fails while incoming reads are paused (such as due to backpressure), the node attempts a send or read that immediately fails, producing misleading error logs and redundant syscalls instead of explicitly logging the hangup.

risk.why: A flaw in socket readiness and error handling could prematurely terminate legitimate P2P or RPC connections.

scope_notes: Most of the diff consists of test framework extensions and new functional tests for socket error handling.
summary: Disconnects sockets immediately in P2P net and HTTP processing when the socket reports an error or hangup on an established connection where reads were not requested. It bypasses an outgoing send attempt that would fail anyway and logs a direct disconnect message. It also adds test coverage for TCP urgent (OOB) bytes and TCP resets while sending.
